content: A hospital network refers to a group of hospitals that collaborate to coordinate and deliver a wide range of healthcare services to the communities they serve. A hospital system, also known as a healthcare system, consists of two or more hospitals that are owned, sponsored, or managed under contract by a central organization. To mitigate financial losses caused by decreasing reimbursements and rising operational costs, as well as to enhance the quality of care and reduce redundancy in services, hospitals may choose to consolidate specific services at a single location. However, this consolidation may require patients to travel greater distances if those services are no longer available at their local hospital. Internationally, several notable hospital networks exist. For example, Adventist Health International operates across 13 countries. Aga Khan Health Services manages nine hospitals in regions including Central and South Asia as well as East Africa. Apollo Hospitals, an Indian healthcare corporation, runs 38 hospitals across South Asia. In Canada, Eastern Health operates seven hospitals, while the Health Care Corporation of St. John's is another prominent healthcare organization.
